reader_opening_policy: Only the personal family dedication before the story. No series synopsis or foreknowledge of later losses.
scope: Childhood home, school, illness, learning, Warsaw, Vienna, recovery and homecoming. Parents’ deaths, wars, farming, aliyah and Esther belong to later volumes.
editorial_frame: The direct address to great-grandchildren is new literary framing requested by the family. The 1971 diary dedication names children and grandchildren. No meeting with great-grandchildren is claimed.
stage_policy: Known events may be staged visually; do not invent a new incident, spoken exchange, promise, failure, rescue or emotional declaration as historical fact.
print_assumption: For planning, story page 1 is a single left page in an RTL book; spreads are 2/3, 4/5 etc. Verify actual front-matter imposition before final art. Reveal pairs must stay separated by a real page turn.
open_questions: Exact ages and dates for foot illness, Warsaw and Vienna.
The Balkan-wars reference and place names are retrospective; do not infer a precise year from them without further research.
The first-school recollection names 1904. Character age must differ from later childhood; the existing child-v02 is not a verified age-four reference.
The timing of Father’s departure relative to surgery in Warsaw is not dated.
The original says Father did not collect Yitzhak on the return from Warsaw; a man from their town did.
The siddur was thrown ON TOP of a tall stove. No burning, retrieval or replacement is recorded.
Which Vienna hospital and synagogue, supporting faces and exact buildings remain unidentified.
lettering_policy: Live Hebrew and English, one scene per image, no AI lettering, generous crop and text margins. Count words after arranging the scene; never abbreviate essential context to hit an arbitrary total.
